headline: SSC pass rate hits 19-year low with nearly 7 lakh students failing
summary: The overall pass rate dropped to 64.05%, the lowest since 2007, with over 500,000 students failing. Weakness in English and Mathematics, along with poor performance in the Humanities division, are cited as major factors.
details: The Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination pass rate has plummeted to 64.05% across nine general education boards, marking the lowest in 19 years. This year, 504,929 students failed to pass, an increase from the previous year, with the number of GPA-5 recipients also decreasing by nearly 19,000.

Analysis of the results highlights significant weaknesses in English and Mathematics, with eight out of nine boards (excluding Cumilla) reporting pass rates below 80% in English. The Humanities division also showed comparatively weaker results, significantly impacting the overall pass rate due to its large number of examinees.

Education sector experts attribute the decline to factors like question patterns, student preparedness, and evaluation methods. They emphasize the urgent need to review learning standards, subject-specific teachers, and learning gaps in schools, especially given that over half a million students failed after nearly a decade of schooling.

The results for the 2026 SSC examinations, along with Dakhil under the Madrasah Education Board and SSC Vocational under the Technical Education Board, were published yesterday, Monday. This comprehensive release covers various educational streams simultaneously.

A total of 106,009 students achieved the highest GPA-5 across the nine general education boards, down from 125,018 last year. Dhaka Education Board led in both GPA-5 and overall pass rate, while Mymensingh Education Board recorded the lowest pass rate.

Female students continued their trend of outperforming males, with a pass rate of nearly 68% compared to approximately 60% for male students. Girls also secured more GPA-5s, with over 58,000 female students achieving the top grade against approximately 47,000 male students.

The SSC examinations were held from April 21 to May 20. Out of 1,404,539 participants across the nine general education boards, 899,610 successfully passed. This means over one-third of the examinees could not clear the exams.

The number of educational institutions with a zero pass rate has also risen, with 57 institutions reporting no successful candidates this year, up from 48 last year. This raises concerns about school-level learning quality and preparedness.

Even the top-performing Dhaka Board saw a decline in English results, with a pass rate of just over 78% this year, compared to nearly 88% last year. The chairman of Dhaka Education Board, Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, confirmed that poor performance in English and Mathematics was the primary cause for the overall dip.

Historically, SSC pass rates have fluctuated, reaching over 80% or even 90% for a long period after 2008, following a 57% rate in 2007. The current two-year consecutive decline, starting from 68.04% last year, necessitates a re-evaluation of assessment methods and student preparation.

Despite the significant drop, Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milan stated that the results were 'beautiful' during the result publication ceremony at the Ministry of Education. He emphasized viewing the results positively.

headline_marked: [[111 killed as 7.4 magnitude earthquake]] strikes western Colombia, toppling buildings
headline: 111 killed as 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes western Colombia, toppling buildings
summary: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, causing widespread destruction, injuring dozens, and trapping many under rubble. The new president declared a national state of emergency.
details: At least 111 people were killed and 87 injured after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia yesterday. The quake knocked down buildings across several cities, with many still trapped in the rubble.

The US Geological Survey reported the quake struck at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar in Choco, a sparsely populated province on Colombia’s Pacific Coast. Despite its epicenter, it was felt in major cities nationwide.
The earthquake caused a tower of Manizales' beloved cathedral to fall over, and many buildings in the city sustained damage. Traffic was paralyzed, and residents feared aftershocks.
In Cali, one of Colombia’s largest cities, over two dozen structures collapsed, leaving people trapped. Mayor Alejandro Eder requested disaster teams from Bogota and Medellin to aid rescue efforts.
Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi confirmed injuries and significant damage in Quibdo, the provincial capital. She also issued warnings to residents about potential aftershocks.

The quake hit just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, presenting his new administration with its first major crisis. Memories of devastating twin earthquakes in neighboring Venezuela in June are still fresh.

President De La Espriella declared a national state of emergency, stating the government has deployed all capabilities to protect lives and assist affected communities. He emphasized that rescuing those trapped under rubble is the first priority.
